description: dashboard — the maintainer's one-shot 'what do I do next' join over GitHub. Read-only.

dashboard.description: What do I do next? One read-only call joining the four a maintainer used to run by hand — clone currency, the default branch's CI, the open-PR board, and worktree occupancy — plus the two facts none of them returned: which PRs are mergeable right now, and which lanes are free. The verdict column is derived from the shared #454 tally and gh-pr's own leg reconciliation (#724/#804): a tally that does not sum to the legs the run declares renders UNKNOWN, never WAITING and never MERGE, and CANCELLED/SKIPPED/TIMED_OUT/NEUTRAL/ACTION_REQUIRED are none of them passes — MERGE requires every leg in the passed bucket, so a state added after this was written falls out as UNKNOWN by construction. Lane occupancy is inferred and carries git-worktrees' three states all the way up: an open PR or an `occupied` tree makes a lane occupied, a lane whose only signal is a `cannot tell` tree is `unknown` and never `free`, and `free` additionally requires that every live worktree in the repo was attributable to some lane — one stray occupancy degrades every otherwise-free lane to `unknown` and names it. A section that could not be fetched prints its heading, says `!! unread` with the reason, and is counted in the footer, so a dashboard missing its board is never readable as a dashboard with an empty board. `next:` names one runnable read op or says 'nothing ready' plainly, and declines outright when the board is unread. Ends on a one-line `[result]` verdict that survives `| tail -1`. Read-only, permanently: nothing spawns, heals, fetches or mutates — clone currency is established with `git ls-remote`, which reads the remote without writing yours. GitHub only; there is no GitLab equivalent and none is half-built (see docs/presets/dashboard.md). The lane vocabulary is configuration, not a literal: set ops.dashboard.lane_prefix in .supertool.json (`lane-` here; `priority:`-style colons elsewhere in the same org). There is no default — unconfigured, the lanes section prints `!! unread` and names the key rather than matching zero labels and rendering that as `0 free, 0 occupied, 0 unknown` (#1007). A configured prefix that matches nothing is its own state too: it reports the empty universe, names any label sharing its stem behind a different separator, and still refuses to call any lane free. Budget SUPERTOOL_DASHBOARD_BUDGET (default 90s), fan-out SUPERTOOL_DASHBOARD_WORKERS (default 8).
